title: Nailstone 43-37776 Memorial
crew_summary: 13 killed including pilot 1Lt. Michael H. Primus
narrative: The bomber was on a training flight from Eye to Liverpool when it ran into trouble near Desford aerodrome. It was fully loaded with bombs and ammunition. Trying to turn to reach Desfords runway it flew low over Barlestone and over the edge of Nailstone before hitting a tree on farmland and exploding, killing all 12 airmen. The aircraft was destroyed in the explosion and subsequent fire. The cause of the problem is not known. memorial_details:
Name: B-17 Flying Fortress Crew
Type: Stone of remembrance
Description: Stone of remembrance with attached plaque.
Inscription: IN MEMORY OF OUR (...)/ 490TH BOMB GROUP FLIGHT CREW ON THE/ B17 FLYING FORTRESS APTLY NAMED HEAVENLY BODY/ 27TH SEPTEMBER 1944 ALL CREW MEMBERS LOST THEIR LIVES (...)/ THIS TRAGIC ACCIDENT/ [crew names inscribed on memorial]/ (...)
Location: At centre of village. Church Gardens Memorial Garden Nailstone Hinckley And Bosworth Leicestershire CV13 0QY England
Grid Ref: SK 41802 07150
Coordinates: 52.661171000000,-1.382990400000
Photos: https://media.iwm.org.uk/ciim5/memorials/17/180/large_50741.jpg; https://media.iwm.org.uk/ciim5/memorials/173/254/large_50741a.jpg; https://media.iwm.org.uk/ciim5/memorials/86/568/3_nailstone.jpg; https://media.iwm.org.uk/ciim5/memorials/86/569/4_nailstone_1.jpg

The plaque is inscribed in English inscribed with a dedication message followed by the list of names of the crew.

The memorial was originally located at a site nearer to where the plane crashed on Elmside Farm but has been moved for better access, where it was dedicated in 2002.

Dedication (2002-01-01): The memorial was dedicated after being moved to its current location for better access.
